titleStmt.title: Shiji 史记 · 秦庄襄王三年: notes

div.interp: The third year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, 247 BC.

The Jijie cites Xu Guang: one text has 波 for 汲, Bo County being also in Henei. The Zhengyi cites the Kuodizhi: the old city of Gaodu is Zezhou; the old city of Ji lies twenty-five li south-west of the Ji County governed from Weizhou.

The Zhengyi cites the Kuodizhi: Yuci is a County of Bingzhou, the ancient Yuci; Xincheng, also called Xiaopingcheng, lies forty-seven li south-west of Shanyang County in Shuozhou; the old city of Langmeng twenty-six li north-east of Yangqu County in Bingzhou. The Table and the Hereditary Houses enter the campaign under the previous year (248 BC, §2, §3).
The Zhengyi: the thirty-seven Fortresses are the lands of the three States of Bingzhou, Daizhou and Shuozhou, in the names of the Tang.
四月日食: the Table enters an eclipse under the previous year (248 BC, §2).
王龁: the Basic Annals' writing of the general whom the Table (§2) and the Suiji call 王齮, Wang Yi; the two are taken as one man.
The Zhengyi: Shangdang had again turned against Qin, hence the attack.
The Zhengyi: all north of Shangdang is Taiyuan land, that is the thirty-seven Fortresses above. The Hereditary House of Yan puts the founding under the previous year (248 BC, §3).
The Zhengyi: Wuji is Lord Xinling; he led the troops of Yan, Zhao, Han, Chu and Wei against Qin.
The Zhengyi: Meng Ao, beaten by the five states' troops, broke off and fell back to Hewai, the States of Shanzhou and Huazhou in the names of the Tang.
子政: Ying Zheng, King of Qin from this accession; the Basic Annals name him by the imperial title he took later.
